To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of heterotic string models with the matter content and the gauge group of the standard model is large, that the number of models with an extra anomalous U(1) symmetry is even larger, that the number with a massless extra U(1) is not negligible and that the number of such models with a spontaneously broken extra U(1), leading to a phenomenologically interesting phenomenology, is also not negligible.

(i) there are many standard-like models in heterotic string theory; (ii) they are characterized by an interesting phenomenology, in particular with regard to the Yukawa sector; (iii) the number of standard-like models can be increased by extending the search to more general manifolds and by including non-standard matter representations

(1) there are many heterotic Calabi-Yau standard models; (2) they are characterized by an intricate pattern of global U(1)-symmetries; (3) these global symmetries can be used to suppress dangerous operators and to stabilize the proton.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of string standard models which, in contrast to the vast majority of previous attempts, are based on a systematic search over the complete intersection Calabi–Yau manifold class.
a detailed study of string phenomenology, in particular with a systematic analysis of string standard model building.
the construction and phenomenological analysis of heterotic standard models.

string theory provides a large number of models which, in principle, could be tested experimentally.
the phenomenology of string standard models is rich and varied and that it can be systematically explored.
string theory is the unique framework for constructing realistic standard model vacua.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of string theory, the MSSM is not an isolated model but rather part of a larger class of models which are related to each other through a number of continuous and discrete symmetries.
, in the absence of any additional structure, the MSSM can be obtained by compactifying the heterotic string on smooth Calabi- Yau three-folds.
we have constructed 200 string models with the same matter content as the MSSM, and that we have shown how to embed these models in a string theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phenomenologically viable heterotic standard models can have very different features, and that a more systematic study of string phenomenology should take these differences into account.
there is no shortage of string standard models with a phenomenologically viable particle spectrum.

there are a large number of string standard models which are consistent with all phenomenological constraints, and which have the potential to address the main problems of particle physics and cosmology in a natural way.
